# NestJS services

Use when authoring NestJS controllers, providers, guards, interceptors, or module boundaries.

## Modules and DI
- Keep services request-stateless (`Scope.DEFAULT` singleton). Request-scoped providers (`Scope.REQUEST`) bubble up the entire dependency tree and allocate per request.
- Export only public module facades; use `forwardRef` only as a last resort when decoupling circular dependencies properly is blocked.
- Register `enableShutdownHooks()` so `onModuleDestroy` and `onApplicationShutdown` drain database pools and queues gracefully.

## Validation and pipeline order
- Enable global `ValidationPipe({ whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true, transform: true })` so unexpected fields never slip into handlers.
- Know the Nest execution sequence: Middleware → Guards → Interceptors (before) → Pipes → Controller → Interceptors (after) → Exception Filters.
- Never catch and swallow database or transport errors silently inside services; map domain errors cleanly to typed HTTP exceptions.

## Security and serialization
Use `ClassSerializerInterceptor` with `@Exclude()` on password/token properties or map explicit response DTOs instead of returning ORM entities directly.

## Verify
Unit tests overriding providers cleanly with `Test.createTestingModule`, plus e2e `supertest` specs exercising guards, whitelist validation rejection, and shutdown cleanup.
